title: Pause the automatic write-off of balances over a year old
detail: Turn off the rule that writes off balances over a year old until each balance has been checked against its filing and appeal limits. Some are still collectible. Approve yourself, in writing, any standing rule that changes a claim's date, code or balance.

title: Set place of service on November's care-management claims from each resident's status
detail: Before the month-end batch goes out, mark each nursing facility resident as in a Medicare Part A stay (place of service 31) or a long-term resident (32), from the facility's list. Assisted living stays 13. In 2026 Medicare allows $142.98 against $80.71 for the first hour and $77.47 against $44.58 for each added half hour. Where a facility has not yet sent its list, leave that facility's lines as they are and correct them when it arrives.

title: Engage a healthcare attorney before the visit-level audit
detail: Do this before anyone reads a chart for the coding audit. Ask your malpractice insurer or the Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service for two attorneys who handle Medicare billing reviews. Ask the attorney to direct the coding audit and any review of past visit claims. A review the attorney directs can be privileged if its results stay with the attorney. Write down the date the attorney is engaged.

title: Withdrawn: attorney-directed look at care-management records
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Withdrawn: comparison of logged minutes with hours worked
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Withdrawn: choice of code per patient from the records
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Make consent and minutes required before a claim is built
detail: The billing routine refuses to create a care-management claim without both.

title: Find out why Medicare denies some care-management lines as the wrong provider type
detail: 38 complex-code lines since June were denied with reason 170 and remark N95. Call First Coast's provider line, or have a staff member call, and ask what triggers it and whether the place of service on the claim is part of it.

title: Check each patient's status before a care-management claim is built
detail: If the patient died, left the practice's care or elected hospice during the month, bill only when the full time was logged before that day. Never use a date of service after the date of death. Mark each resident's place of service from the facility's list: 31 in a Part A skilled stay, 32 otherwise.

title: Write down where each kind of record is kept
detail: List visit notes, care plans, consents and care-management time logs. For each, name the system or facility that holds it and who can pull a copy. Confirm the practice can get a copy of any note when a payer asks for it.

title: Withdrawn: attorney's written advice on care-management claims already paid
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Have the attorney set, in writing, the dates that govern any refund
detail: The rule gives 60 days to report and return an overpayment once it is identified. A prompt, good-faith review of related claims pauses that deadline, for no more than 180 days after the first overpayment was identified (title 42 of the Code of Federal Regulations, section 401.305). The attorney decides when each clock starts. As an outer guide only: counted from this report, November 10, 2026, day 60 is January 9, 2027 and day 180 is May 9, 2027. Put the attorney's dates on the calendar, and send any audit finding of an overpayment to the attorney the same week.

title: Write one page on why revenue fell from 2023 to 2025
detail: List the sites, services and staff that were lost and why, and what brought revenue back in 2026. A buyer or a lender will ask, and the budget needs it.

title: Have the attorney engage a certified outside auditor
detail: Ask for experience with hospital and nursing facility visits and for both over- and under-coding findings.

title: Have the auditor draw the random sample
detail: The software gives the auditor a list of every visit claim from the last six months. The auditor picks 10 notes per code family per clinician, about 80 to 100 notes.

title: Send the notes securely
detail: Clinical notes come from the health record, not from the billing database.

title: Review the report with the attorney, then with both clinicians as the attorney advises
detail: Agree what changes in how levels are chosen and documented.

title: Schedule the quarterly 10-chart audit
detail: Same auditor, both clinicians, results logged.

title: Ask the auditor to include 10 advance care planning notes
detail: Advance care planning has a high national error rate for missing documentation of time.

title: List every initial nursing facility visit billed under the nurse practitioner since May 1, 2026
detail: Start after the attorney is engaged. The software drafts the list from claims. Ask each facility which of these residents were in a Medicare Part A skilled stay. For those, the physician writes down from the chart the date of his own comprehensive visit, or that none was found. Give the list to the attorney.

title: Write down how a visit level gets from the note to the claim, and what changed in 2024 and in 2026
detail: Do this for the attorney, after the attorney is engaged. The physician's share of top-level hospital follow-ups was 64.5% in 2023, 1.3% in 2024 and 73.7% now. For each period record who picked the code, in which tool, and whether the tool offers a default level. Do the same for how patients get onto the monthly care-management list. The attorney shares it with the auditor.

title: Add a monthly table of each clinician's level mix against the national mix to the scorecard
detail: For each code family, show the share billed at each level beside the national share.

title: Hold a coding education session built from the audit's findings
detail: Use what the attorney agrees to share from the audit. Both clinicians attend. Record the date and who was there.

title: Add a time statement and the required elements to the advance care planning note
detail: At least 16 minutes of discussion is needed to bill it. The note states the minutes, who took part and that the talk was voluntary. Those minutes are not counted toward the visit billed the same day. From January 1, 2027 code 99497 covers only time the billing clinician personally spent. Time spent by staff uses new codes G0572 and G0573.

title: Ask each of the five nursing facilities for a weekly census with payer, skilled-stay status and the start and end date of each skilled stay
detail: The business office produces this already for its own billing.

title: Store skilled-stay, hospice and plan status by date
detail: New fields on the patient record in the database.

title: Set place of service 31 or 32 from the census
detail: Applies to visits and to care management. In 2026 Medicare allows $114.90 against $99.58 for a follow-up visit under code 32, and $142.98 against $80.71 for the first hour of complex care management. Ask First Coast in writing whether care management may be billed for a month in which the resident was in a Medicare Part A skilled stay. A 2016 Medicare question-and-answer sheet said no. The current one, last updated in 2022, says care management can be billed for nursing facility residents and does not repeat that limit.

title: Count how many of the past year's claims carried the wrong setting
detail: By month, code and payer, with the payment difference in each direction and the date each claim was first paid. This sizes the look-back.

title: Decide whether to ask Medicare to reopen claims billed as skilled stays for long-term residents
detail: A paid claim is corrected by a reopening request to First Coast that changes the place of service, through its SPOT portal (Secure Provider Online Tool) or its Reopening Gateway. The limit is one year from the date the claim was first paid, so the oldest claims reach it soon. After a year First Coast reopens only for good cause and may refuse. Weigh the money against the attention: a batch of requests that each raise payment invites Medicare to look at those claims, and a reopened claim can be reviewed again. Before any claim is changed, have the facility's stay dates on file for that resident, apply one written rule to every affected claim, and start with a small batch. A person sends each batch. Do not net money recovered this way against any refund owed on other claims.

title: Ask each nursing facility for every resident's skilled-stay start and end dates since January 1, 2026
detail: The weekly census shows today only. Past dates are needed to tell which 2026 visits carried the wrong setting.

title: Clear the 342 coverage cards still in work
detail: Electronic check first, portal second, facility business office third.

title: Run eligibility for every active patient on December 1
detail: Then on the first of every month. Flag plan changes, hospice and new secondary coverage.

title: Hold any claim with no verified payer and list it daily
detail: Replace silent no-payer charges with a short daily list.

title: Get portal access for the Medicaid long-term care plan with $26,640 open
detail: It allows eligibility only through its portal and pays by paper check.

title: Count how many charges entered with no payer were never paid
detail: Take October's charges that had no payer when entered. Report how many now have a payer, how many were paid, and the dollars still unpaid.

title: Compare each day's visits by site with the charges entered, and list the gaps
detail: A visit on the census with no charge goes on a short daily list.

title: Sort the correct-and-resend list by each payer's filing deadline
detail: Medicare: one year from the date of service. Florida Medicaid plans: six months from the date of service when the plan pays first. When Medicare pays first, the state's plan contract allows three years from the date of service. When another insurer pays first, 90 days from that insurer's final decision. Ask each plan which of these it applies when a Medicare Advantage plan pays first. Florida Medicaid itself, after Medicare: 12 months from the date of service or six months after Medicare's decision, whichever is later. Other plans: the contract. Check each plan's provider manual before treating any claim as too late. These limits are for sending a claim the first time. A Medicare claim that was denied is usually fixed by a reopening request within one year of the decision or an appeal within 120 days of it. Only a claim Medicare returned as incomplete is sent again.

title: Work the 74 actionable denials worth $13,463
detail: From the latest billing run. Leave out any fix that changes a code, a date, a modifier, a diagnosis or the place of service until a person has approved it.

title: Dispute recent denials coded as not payable under a managed care contract
detail: 32 recent lines carry this code: 21 top-level hospital follow-ups, plus hospital and nursing facility admissions. First find which plan sent each one, whether the practice is in that plan's network, and whether the denial is still inside the plan's dispute window.

title: Report receivables by age and payer every Monday
detail: One table on the dashboard.

title: Report denials by cause and payer each month
detail: One table on the dashboard. Pick one cause to fix each month.

title: File the physician's Florida Medicaid provider agreement renewal
detail: Due December 1, 2026. File this week. Thanksgiving leaves few working days before the deadline. Ask for written confirmation that the renewal is complete, not only received, and ask what happens to claims if approval comes after December 1. Use the nurse practitioner's returned filing to see what the agency rejects.

title: Resubmit the nurse practitioner's Medicaid revalidation
detail: It was returned incomplete. Ask the agency exactly what was missing. The nurse practitioner signs it.

title: Correct the nurse practitioner's national provider record
detail: Current address and the right specialty code.

title: Enroll with Railroad Medicare
detail: A separate contractor, Palmetto GBA, handles Railroad Medicare. Have a person at the practice ask it how enrollment works and what the effective date will be. Stop writing off these claims until that is known, because a claim may be filed up to one year after the date of service. $3,764 is open.

title: Resolve the terminated commercial plan
detail: Confirm in writing whether the physician is participating, and re-apply if not.

title: Finish Veterans Affairs portal registration and the military plan's credentialing of the nurse practitioner
detail: The nurse practitioner signs her own application. The software can prepare the forms.

title: Build one expiry calendar for both clinicians
detail: Licenses, registrations, board certification, privileges, every payer enrollment, and the nurse practitioner's protocol (or autonomous practice registration) with its date. Include each clinician's re-attestation date for the shared credentialing profile (CAQH), which lapses after 120 days, and each Medicare revalidation due date from Medicare's revalidation list: a missed revalidation means unpaid visits from the due date.

title: Close the open items on the hospital reappointment
detail: Call the medical staff office this week. Ask for the list of what is missing and the date the current appointment ends, then send everything. The hospital is 37.8% of charges.

title: Complete the overdue UnitedHealthcare directory attestation
detail: UnitedHealthcare and its plan for people with Medicare and Medicaid hold $48,140 of open receivables.

title: Complete the overdue required training for the Sunshine plan
detail: Ask the plan which clinician it lists as overdue, and keep the completion record.

title: Fix the military plan's rejected enrollment for electronic claims, and get an authorization number before each Veterans Affairs visit is billed
detail: Resubmit the enrollment and get written confirmation. Hold each Veterans Affairs claim until its authorization number is on it.

title: Explain the $12,902 of Medicare deposits with no remittance
detail: Find and post the remittances.

title: Chase the large plan whose remittances arrived with no money
detail: Call the plan this week. Ask how each payment since August was sent. If it was sent as a one-time card number, ask for it to be reissued and switch to bank deposit. The software lists the remittances that have no matching deposit.

title: Complete electronic remittance and deposit enrollment for every payer
detail: Including the plan whose enrollment was rejected. The software prepares each form. The owner signs it and confirms the bank account.

title: Have the accountant reconcile the bank account monthly
detail: Someone other than the person, or the software, that posts payments.

title: Re-authorize the accounting software connection
detail: So monthly results can load into the practice database.

title: Agree a monthly close by the 15th with the accountant
detail: Income statement, balance sheet and a cash summary.

title: Build the 2027 budget with four scenarios
detail: Steady, loss of the largest site, a second nurse practitioner, and care-management collections falling by half. Price the 2027 Medicare changes code by code, not as a flat 2.31% cut: hospital visits fall 3% to 5% and nursing facility visits billed as a skilled stay rise 10% to 12%.

title: Hold the first monthly review
detail: Scorecard, work list, cash, and one decision recorded.

title: Pull payments, adjustments and write-offs by month of service
detail: From the billing system, to compute the net collection rate.

title: Name one person to keep this work list
detail: A staff member or an outside project manager keeps the list, chases each item and reports to you each week. Until mid-December keep for yourself only what needs your judgment or signature: engaging the attorney, signing the Medicaid renewal, approving which billing rules are switched off, and deciding the care-management code once the attorney-directed sample is done. Hand the facility calls, the plan portal access and the accounting link to that person or to the nurse practitioner. Leave the database key change with whoever already administers the database.

title: Write a compliance program of a few pages with the attorney
detail: The seven elements from federal guidance, scaled down.

title: Collect every medical director agreement from the past six years, with fair-market-value support and time logs
detail: For the attorney's review. Two are active in 2026. Five or more were active in 2023, when stipends were $185,300. Stipends were $54,000 in 2024 and $96,500 in 2025. Include agreements that have ended, with the end date and the reason. Start a monthly time log for the two active ones now.

title: Do a security risk analysis
detail: Assess the risks to all electronic patient information the practice holds: where it is stored and sent, who and what can reach it (including the software agents and their keys), what could go wrong, how likely and how serious it is, and what will be done about each risk. Include the vendor list, each business associate agreement and where each vendor stores data. Have someone other than the billing agent review and sign it. The free federal Security Risk Assessment Tool at healthit.gov is built for small practices. The owner signs and dates the result.

title: Have the auditor read the billing rulebook's high-risk rules
detail: Any rule that changes a code, date, modifier, diagnosis, place of service or balance.

title: Name one person to receive record requests and log deadlines
detail: Pick the person who opens the mail and the payer portals each business day. Log each request the day it arrives: who sent it, which claims, the due date and what was sent back.

title: Add a required-visit due date for every nursing facility resident
detail: Every 30 days for the first 90 days, then every 60 days, each with 10 days of grace. Record who must make each visit: in a Medicare Part A skilled stay the physician makes the first visit and at least every other required visit. For other residents Florida's rule allows another licensed professional. Ask the attorney whether that covers the first visit.

title: Get a written statement of where each vendor stores patient information
detail: Florida requires patient information kept offsite or in the cloud to stay in the continental United States, its territories or Canada. Ask every software and AI vendor.

title: Record yearly compliance training for both clinicians
detail: One hour is enough. Keep the date, the topics and the names.

title: Have the attorney read the nurse practitioner's employment agreement and her Florida practice protocol
detail: Florida requires a written protocol kept at each place she practices, unless she is registered for autonomous practice.

title: Check that every Advance Beneficiary Notice form is the current version
detail: Since May 12, 2026 only the form marked 'Exp. 03/31/2029' is valid for Original Medicare. Check the templates in the record system, any paper copies each clinician carries and any packets a facility supplies. The notice is required when Medicare is likely to deny a service as not medically necessary, such as a wellness visit repeated too soon. An old form on such a denial can leave the write-off with the practice. Raised by the vendor's newsletter and checked against Medicare's own announcement.

title: Turn off open sign-up on this application
detail: A check added on November 10, 2026 refuses any account whose address has not been confirmed. Before that, an account needed only an approved address. Read the access log for sign-ins nobody recognizes, confirm that the approved address's account belongs to its owner, and write down what was found. Then turn off open sign-up. The access log was read on November 10, 2026: 31 requests, all on November 7, all from the one confirmed account, and none refused. Only one account exists.

title: Replace the database access key that was pasted into a chat
detail: Revoke it in the database console today and issue a new one. Then read the database's connection and query logs for the days the key was exposed, and write down what was found and what was done. If the console shows no logs, ask the database vendor for them. If the logs show access nobody can explain, tell the attorney, because the breach notification rules may apply.

title: Require the owner's written approval for any rule that changes a claim's code, date, modifier, diagnosis, place of service or balance
detail: The software builds the check and lists the rules. You approve each one in writing before it runs.

title: Sample 25 automated actions each month and record the result
detail: The correction rate becomes a scorecard measure.

title: Make every write-off carry a reason code, and keep patient balances out of the automatic rule
detail: Routine waiver of Medicare copayments and deductibles is unlawful, and billing a Qualified Medicare Beneficiary for them is forbidden. The automatic rule should touch insurance balances only. A patient balance is written off only with a reason: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary, documented hardship, or unpaid after documented attempts to collect.

title: Run a credit balance report, and confirm the November 2 write-off touched only amounts owed to the practice
detail: List every account where a payer or patient is owed money. Check that none of the $40,686 written off was a credit. The owner reviews the list.

title: Look up both clinicians in the participation status tool
detail: Use each clinician's national provider number.

title: Read the latest performance feedback and payment adjustment
detail: Nothing has to be submitted for this step: it is to read what Medicare has already decided. Sign in at qpp.cms.gov this week. Medicare released the 2025 scores and the 2027 payment adjustment on September 21, 2026. The page shows whether each clinician was scored, whether the physician was scored on the hospital's results, and the cut or bonus for 2027. A request for Medicare to review a score must be filed before the review window closes. Medicare's guide says it closes 30 days after the payment adjustments were released, and specialty society notices put that at about 60 days after September 21, so around November 20, 2026. Confirm the date on the site. If a penalty is shown for 2027, put it in the budget.

title: Choose how to report for 2026
detail: Decide by early December. A practice with 15 or fewer clinicians is excused from the electronic health record category without applying. Quality for 2026 can still be reported after the year ends, for example through a qualified registry, if the notes hold the data. An improvement activity counts only if it ran 90 days in a row within 2026. The exception application is only for events outside the practice's control and closes December 31, 2026. Submission is due March 31, 2027.

title: Submit 2026 quality data
detail: The submission window at qpp.cms.gov opens January 4, 2027 and closes March 31, 2027. Aim to finish two weeks early.

title: List long-term residents with no wellness visit in the last 12 months
detail: Use the census and the billing history. Mark any resident whose last wellness visit date is not known.

title: Schedule wellness visits, about a dozen a month
detail: Work from the list, one facility at a time.

title: Set up a transitional care routine for discharges to assisted living or home
detail: Contact within two business days and a visit within 7 or 14 days.

title: Reset the fee schedule each January
detail: Every charge above the highest contracted rate. This needs the contract rates, which are due by the end of February. The software drafts the schedule and the owner approves it.

title: Request the current contract and fee schedule from every plan
detail: Write to each plan's provider relations office. Ask for the signed contract, every amendment and the current fee schedule for the practice's codes.

title: Load the 2027 Medicare fee schedule for the practice's locality
detail: Medicare published the 2027 values in November 2026. First Coast posts the fees for each Florida area in its Fee Schedule Lookup.

title: Reprice the top 15 codes at 2027 rates by site of service
detail: Show the change per code and in total.

title: Flag any payment below the expected amount
detail: Compare each paid line with the loaded fee schedule and list the differences each week.

title: Confirm 2027 network status with each Medicare Advantage plan
detail: Plans set their 2027 networks and benefits in mid-2026, and Medicare published the 2027 star ratings on October 8, 2026. Ask each plan in writing whether both clinicians stay in network for 2027. Look up each plan's rating on Medicare's plan finder: a plan under 4 stars loses a bonus and a plan under 3.5 gets a smaller rebate share, and those plans tend to tighten authorization and payment. Raised by the vendor's newsletter and checked against Medicare's rules.

title: Get two refinance quotes for the $187,206 note
detail: Check the note for a prepayment charge first.

title: Agree a plan to retire the $162,121 owed by the owner
detail: Repayment, pay or distribution, and the tax effect of each.

title: Review the owner's salary against market pay
detail: Reasonable compensation for an S corporation owner.

title: Set a cash floor and start a 13-week cash forecast
detail: A cash floor is the lowest bank balance you allow before owner draws pause. Ninety days of spending is about $177,000, and cash was $94,431 on September 30, 2026. Agree with the accountant what owner distributions are paid until the floor is reached and the care-management sample has been read. A 13-week forecast is one row a week of expected deposits and payments. Ask the accountant for a template.

title: Ask the broker about cyber and billing-audit defense cover
detail: Call the malpractice insurer and the insurance broker this week. Ask whether the current policy pays for the defense of a billing audit, and whether it requires an attorney from the insurer's list. Ask only what the policy covers. Leave any description of the reviews to the attorney.

title: Tell the accountant about any personal tax balance, and include it when asking for loan quotes
detail: Any personal tax balance owed to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and any payment plan on it, is outside the practice. It still bears on distributions, on any refinance and on a sale.

title: Ask the bank for a line of credit
detail: The risk review lists an unused line of credit as a control. Ask while 2026 results are strong.

title: Write a two-page emergency plan
detail: Who covers patients, who can sign, who has access to bank and systems, and who can pause the billing software if you are away. Add who would tell patients and facilities, and who would keep the records, if the practice had to stop.

title: Sign a mutual coverage agreement with another physician
detail: Ask a physician who already sees patients at the same hospital or facilities. Put in writing who covers whom, for how long and how each is paid.

title: Start a relationship record for each site
detail: Decision makers, last contact, what they want, any agreement and its end date.

title: Review disability, key-person and business overhead insurance
detail: Ask the insurance broker what each policy would pay if you could not work for three months.

title: Introduce the nurse practitioner to the administrator at each site
detail: Start with the three largest sites.

title: List every nursing and assisted living facility within 40 minutes
detail: Beds, current physician coverage and a contact.

title: Build the hiring case
detail: Six-month ramp, three-month enrollment delay, cost and break-even census.

title: Decide, and if yes start enrollment the day the offer is signed
detail: Use the hiring case. Decide only after the coding audit is finished.

title: Open a data room folder with the standard sections
detail: Financial, contracts, billing reports, compliance, people, systems.

title: Separate recurring collections from recovery of old receivables each month
detail: Use payment dates and dates of service, together with the month-of-service pull in the monthly close project. Do not rely on the valuation until this is done.

title: Choose a target year for stepping back
detail: Plan three to five years ahead.

title: Refresh the valuation with a full year of clean numbers
detail: Use twelve months of monthly statements and the split of recurring and one-time collections.
